$comment: Pinned toolchain for building and testing the native layer in APK/src. build-apk.sh, test-apk.sh and CI all read this file, so a version changes in one place. Every download is checked against its sha256 before use. jdkMajor is the newest LTS JDK and only compiles; the phone runs ART, not a JVM. javaTarget is the source and bytecode level; above 8, javac compiles against a system image built from the platform's core-for-system-modules.jar (as the Android Gradle Plugin does), so only APIs Android actually has will compile. d8 desugars the result for the minSdkVersion in android/apktool.yml, and buildTools must be new enough for d8 to read that class file version (35.0.0 stops at Java 21; 37.0.0 reads 25). Changing jdkMajor, javaTarget, buildTools or apktool can change the compiled classes.dex; after bumping one, run ./APK/build-apk.sh --no-sign and commit the rebuilt APK/android/classes.dex.

emulator.$comment: The virtual phone APK/apk-dev.mjs emulator creates and boots: the Android version and screen of the owner's Pixel 10, so a check on it means the same thing as a check on the phone.
